concepts.title: The Other Side of Zero: Negative Numbers
concepts.definition: Below zero lies the other side of the number line: numbers less than zero, written with a minus sign, arise from temperatures below freezing, steps to the left of a starting point, or giving away tokens one does not have.
concepts.key_idea: Zero is the floor between two worlds: one side counts what we have, the other counts what we owe.

concepts.title: Moves on the Number Line: Adding Integers
concepts.definition: On the number line, adding a positive number moves the token right and adding a negative number moves it left; the landing point of the token is the sum of the start and the signed move.
concepts.key_idea: Addition is motion: sign decides direction, size decides distance, and the token lands on the sum.
concepts.textbook_ref: fegp110.txt, Moving on the number line

solution_steps.explain: Place the token at the starting number on the number line.
Add the move with its sign; the token lands on the total.

concepts.title: Adding Positive and Negative Numbers
concepts.definition: When a positive and a negative number are added, the bigger magnitude wins the sign and the difference gives the size: 5 plus -3 lands at 2, while 3 plus -5 lands at -2.
concepts.key_idea: Opposite pulls cancel partially: subtract the magnitudes and keep the sign of the larger pull.

concepts.title: Back and Forth: Subtraction and Undoing
concepts.definition: Every move can be undone: moving 4 right and then 4 left returns to the start, so subtraction is the reverse move of addition, and pairs like +4 and -4 wipe each other out.
concepts.key_idea: Plus and minus are mirrors in motion: the reverse move undoes exactly what the first move did.
